title.narrative: Streamlining efficiencies in water tankering markets in emerging cities through data

description.narrative: Powwater intends to solve operational inefficiencies inherent in Nairobi’s highly fragmented water tankering market to improve access to reliable, affordable, and high-quality water for consumers. This will be achieved through: · IoT integration of sensor technologies and hardware for real-time monitoring of groundwater levels and quality· Fleet management - This entails building an IoT-enabled, smart water truck fleet management system with sensors technologies for fuel management and network optimization.· GPS truck route support, aligned with background calculations of groundwater-level data, water quality data, and contextual water-demand data for improved drivers’ logistical decisions.The project aims to enable the distribution of at least 250 million liters of high-quality water to 50,000 additional consumers in Nairobi supplied by Powwater and 5 other water tankering drivers outside their network.

title.narrative: Please provide a short narrative explanation of the data here. (max 250 words)

actual.value: 2024 was marked by significant achievements, including: 1. The development of sensor prototypes for pH, TDS, and water level monitoring, 2. Successful installation and calibration across 20 fill sites, and 3. Integration of sensor readings with initial tech dashboards for real-time monitoring. We provided mandatory WASH training to borehole owners and truck drivers who now have the hygiene knowledge on borehole water handling. We also conducted impactful fluoride training sessions for borehole owners and customers, addressing concerns about fluoride levels in Nairobi's water. From October to December, we made significant progress in refining the automation model for truck delivery optimization. We completed eight phases of enhancement. These refinements yielded impressive results, with average delivery times decreasing markedly. In October, automated deliveries took an average of 6 to 7 hours, but by December, this figure had dropped to under 2.5 hours across all trucks, reflecting a dramatic improvement in operational efficiency. During Q4, the average monthly earnings of borehole owners stood at $2,538, from $1,321 in the previous quarter, demonstrating the viability of our shared economy for water model. Business growth reached record highs, with September 2024 being our highest volume month ever, delivering nearly 30 million liters of water. In October, November and December, we delivered 28,695,000 liters, 20,630,000 liters 19,165,000 liters respectively. The decline in November and December sales is attributed to seasonal factors, including the rainy season and the festive period, which typically shift consumer priorities and affect demand.
